name: Differential / Transfer Case Fluid
primaryScope: PRIMARY found for: (a) BMW TIS text for the rear differential oil check/fill (5series.net PDF carrying BMW AG TIS footers and operation codes 33 11 3AZ/9AZ): remove the filler plug, check the level, fill to the lower edge of the filler plug opening, use only approved gear oils; plug torque table 3AZ (oil fill/drain plug with sealing ring) 65 Nm and 9AZ (plugs with O-ring, replace plugs) 60 Nm. The table lists series E30 to E86 and does NOT name the E90, so it applies to the E90 by plug-type match only; (b) OE parts catalog (RealOEM PH73 USA 09/2009): final drive housing type 188L, ratios 3.23 (row not tied to an option) and 3.73 (automatic S205A), one screw plug with O-ring M22x1.5 33117525064, synthetic gear oil 1 L 83222365987 (valid to 07/2011), no front differential or transfer case groups for this 328i; (c) BMW AG training doc ST502 Powertrain: 188L final drive, lifetime-fill differential oil, ratio table. NO primary found for: rear differential capacity (TIS text and owner manual give none), open vs limited-slip confirmation, service interval, or any xDrive value.
summary: Closed since pass 1: (1) Plug torque: BMW TIS text (via a forum PDF) gives 60 Nm for oil filler/drain plugs WITH an O-ring (replace the plug) and 65 Nm for plugs with a sealing ring; the OE catalog lists the E90 plug as "screw plug with O-ring" (33117525064), so 60 Nm (44 ft-lb) applies, matching bimmersport (E90), bavmods (E9X) and FCP (F30). The earlier E60 poster's claim of 65 Nm with O-ring / 60 Nm without is reversed relative to the TIS table. Caveat: the TIS table does not name the E90 and says replace the plug. (2) Fill method now has a PRIMARY: fill to the lower edge of the filler opening; single filler/drain plug confirmed by 4 sources and one screw plug in the catalog. (3) Capacity: 1.0 L for the N52 (bimmerpost, bimmersport, 5series N52 poster; measured 0.95 L out and 1.1 L in) versus 1.2 L for the N54/335i/diesel (bimmerpost, bimmersport) and a generic bavmods 1.2 L; status VERIFIED_SECONDARY about 1.0 L, but the level at the opening governs (BMW TIS). (4) Fluid: OE catalog lists synthetic gear oil 83222365987 and Turner cross-references it to SAF-XO 75W-90 GL-5 07512293972 (also listed by ECS and FCP); FCP says 75W-140 only for M3/LSD. (5) Open vs limited-slip: nothing in the OE catalog or BMW training doc for this 328i indicates an LSD (single rear axle assembly listed with only ratio variants); 75W-140 is for M3/LSD cars per FCP. Not proven for the VIN, so one owner check remains. (6) Drive type: the catalog model 328i has no front differential or transfer case groups, indicating RWD; xDrive content is therefore out of scope for this VIN and kept only as reference data (transfer case DTF-1, about 1 L; front differential 60 Nm and 700-1000 ml are from F30 data, not E90). (7) Service interval: BMW training says lifetime-fill; retailers/forums say 40,000-60,000 mi or 75,000-100,000 km; no BMW scheduled interval found. Pass 4 (remote only): open differential now rests on four lines of evidence (catalog, VIN decode, Turner, BimmerWorld) so the owner no longer needs to inspect it; final-drive ratio recorded as 3.73 automatic / 3.23 catalog with 3.46 explicitly NOT found; automatic transmission fluid documented as a separate sealed unit not covered here (BMW 'lifetime' vs ZF/GM intervals, transmission model unproven); xDrive items marked not applicable. Still open: BMW capacity figure (1.0 L vs 1.2 L, level governs), BMW service interval, E90-named TIS torque table (60 Nm is primary by plug-type match). Usable as an UNCERTIFIED draft.
variantDependencies: Drive type: OE catalog model 328i lists only a rear axle drive (final drive 188L) and no front axle differential, front drive shaft or transfer case; VIN positions 4-6 (PH7) match the catalog type code PH73. RWD is therefore indicated; xDrive (328xi) would add a front differential and ATC transfer case (not applicable, not verified for this VIN).

Ratio/transmission: final drive ratio 3.23 (catalog row not tied to an option, likely non-automatic) and 3.73 with automatic (S205A) per the OE catalog; both are TYP 188L; sources do not show capacity differing by ratio.
Engine/model: 1.0 L is cited for N52 cars and 1.2 L for N54, diesel and 335i cars (bimmerpost, bimmersport); 328i N52 is the 1.0 L group.
Plug type: the catalog lists a screw plug with O-ring for the E90 188L; the BMW TIS torque table uses different values (60 Nm O-ring, 65 Nm sealing ring) by plug type.
Access: bimmerpost (E93 328i) says the plug can be obstructed by lower braces; a snub-nose 14 mm hex or crowfoot may be needed.

Open vs limited-slip: RESOLVED to 'open, probable'. No LSD option in the VIN decode, no LSD variant in the OE catalog for this car, Turner states BMW dropped true limited-slip on the E9X (M3 excepted), and BimmerWorld sells the 328i 3.73 as an open carrier with LSD units as a separate upgrade. The 75W-140 fluid is for M3/LSD cars only and does not apply.

DECODED CONFIG: rear-wheel drive automatic (S205), no limited-slip option code. Decoded from the VIN by one free decoder (bimmer.work, 2026-10-10), cross-checked by NHTSA (328i 3.0 L sedan, not xDrive) and the RealOEM PH73 catalog (no front differential or transfer case groups). Treat as probable.

Final-drive ratio: catalog 3.73 for automatic (S205A), 3.23 otherwise; 3.46 was not found in any source and is not asserted. The ratio does not change the fluid, the filler/drain plug (M22x1.5 with O-ring) or the 60 Nm value in any source.

Transfer case and front differential: NOT APPLICABLE. They exist only on xDrive; this is a 328i (NHTSA decode and catalog show no front axle). Step 8 is kept only as a stop sign for a mis-identified xDrive car.

Automatic transmission fluid: NOT part of this guide. It is a separate sealed unit with its own fill/drain, 'lifetime' per BMW but with shorter intervals from ZF and GM; the transmission model (GA6L45R vs GA6HP19Z) was not proven for this VIN.

tools.item: 14 mm hex (Allen) socket, 1/2 in drive; breaker bar may be needed; snub-nose or short bit if lower braces block access
tools.note: bimmerpost E93 poster: no room to loosen the plug because of the lower braces; crowfoot with the Allen socket used.

tools.item: Torque wrench able to read 60 Nm / 44 ft-lb
Fluid transfer/extraction pump with a tube small enough for the fill hole
tools.note: All describe pumping old oil out through the fill hole because there is no separate drain plug.

tools.item: Hand pump or squeeze bottle to refill through the fill hole
Measuring jug to record extracted volume
Jack stands, ramps or lift on level ground
tools.note: Generic safety equipment; sources are E90 jacking guides (rated stands, level ground). Not diff-specific.

tools.item: Rag/brake cleaner to clean the plug and area

parts.item: BMW SAF-XO 75W-90 GL-5 synthetic gear oil, 1 L
parts.partNumber: 07512293972 (retail); OE catalog: 83222365987 "BMW synthetic OSP 1L", valid up to 07/2011
parts.note: Turner cross-references 83222365987 and 33117525064 on the fluid page (catalog quirk). OE catalog confirms the 1 L synthetic oil for this selection; the SAF-XO spec name comes from retailers, a 5series poster citing the Bentley manual and a bimmerpost poster.

parts.item: Rear differential oil filler/drain screw plug with O-ring, M22x1.5
parts.note: OE catalog item 03 in the final drive gasket set diagram: "screw plug with O-ring". Replace the plug each time per BMW TIS text for O-ring plugs. Turner kit sells it as Rein 33117525064~REN.

parts.item: Magnetic M22x1.5 plug (aftermarket options): ECS 009314ECS01A, Rein HWU0065

parts.note: Catalog sells the plug with O-ring as one part; a forum poster cites a McMaster-Carr Viton O-ring (9263K587).

parts.item: BMW 75W-140 differential fluid, 5 L (M3/LSD cars only)
xDrive only (not applicable to this VIN): DTF-1 transfer case fluid, 1 L
parts.note: BimmerWorld lists 328xi fitment, SAE 75W, API GL-4, "just under 1 liter"; reference only.

fluids.spec: BMW synthetic hypoid gear oil: SAE 75W-90, API GL-5 (Castrol SAF-XO). BMW TIS: use only approved gear oils; other oils can cause serious damage. Open-differential evidence for the 328i: RealOEM lists one final-drive assembly (188L) with only ratio variants for this car; Turner (E9X limited-slip category page) states BMW stopped using truly limited-slip differentials with the E9X and E60 platforms and sells only a ratio swap there; BimmerWorld sells the E9X 325i/328i 3.73 as an open carrier and sells limited-slip versions separately as an upgrade. No 328i LSD option code was found in the VIN decode.
About 1.0 L for N52 cars; about 1.2 L is quoted for 335i/N54/diesel and in a generic E9X article. The BMW TIS text gives no volume: the level at the lower edge of the filler opening governs.
fluids.capacity: 1.0 L (bimmerpost: "1 liter in rear diff with N52"; bimmersport: "1.2 litres for a 335i, all others 1 litre", measured 0.95 L out, about 1.1 L in; 5series E61 N52 poster 1.0 L; xoutpost X5 about 95 percent of a 1 L bottle) vs 1.2 L (bavmods E9X, bimmerpost for N54/diesel)
fluids.dissent: bavmods says 1.2 L for "this E9X model" without naming the engine and says BMW diffs typically hold 1 to 1.4 L.

fluids.spec: 75W-140 per FCP Euro for M3 or LSD cars. No evidence an LSD is fitted to a 328i.
fluids.note: Not applicable to this car: no source shows a factory LSD on the 328i (see open-differential row). Retained for reference only; do not use 75W-140 on this car.

fluids.spec: BMW training doc (ST502): differential oil is lifetime-fill. Retailers/forums: 40,000-60,000 mi (bavmods), 75,000-100,000 km (bimmersport), transfer case every 5th engine oil service (BimmerWorld).
fluids.note: No BMW scheduled interval found. Status honest: BMW training says lifetime fill, retailers and forums say 40,000-60,000 mi; no BMW interval exists. The guide treats a change as owner-optional maintenance, not a BMW requirement.

fluids.item: Front differential (xDrive only; not applicable to this VIN)
fluids.capacity: F30: roughly 700-800 ml or just under 1 L (FCP); E83 X3 forum: about 1 L each diff; none for the E90.

fluids.item: Transfer case (xDrive only; not applicable to this VIN)
fluids.capacity: just under 1 L (BimmerWorld, 328xi); about 1 L (X5 E70); less than 1 L (X3 E83)

fluids.item: Rear differential final-drive ratio (identification only; does not change fluid, capacity or plug torque)
fluids.spec: OE catalog: 3.73 with automatic (S205A) and 3.23 (row not tied to an option, likely manual) on the 188L final drive. BimmerWorld: stock E9X 328i ratio is 3.23 (manual context). Turner: stock manual gearing 3.15 or 3.23. A ratio of 3.46 was checked and appears in none of these sources, so it is NOT asserted for this car. The 3.73 for the automatic is catalog-level inference from the VIN decode, not proven for the VIN.
fluids.note: The ratio is only an identification detail. All fluid/plug facts in this guide hold for either catalog ratio on the 188L housing.

fluids.item: Automatic transmission fluid (separate sealed unit; NOT serviced by this guide)
fluids.spec: The automatic's fluid is not the differential oil and is not changed by this procedure; the transmission has its own pan, fill plug and fluid. BMW treats it as 'lifetime' fill; FCP says BMW's rating is about 100,000 miles, ZF's own interval for 6HP units is 8 years/80,000 km (about 50,000 mi) and GM's service data for the 6L45 is under 45,000 mi; Turner repeats ZF's 50,000 mi or 8 years. Which unit is in this car was not proven: ECS lists both GA6HP19Z (ZF) and GA6L45R (GM) kits for the E90 328i N52, and BimmerWorld lists the GM GA6L45R as used on 328i from 9/2008, so this 09/2009 build is probably the GA6L45R.
fluids.capacity: MISSING (not researched for this guide; Turner's ZF kit is 7 L of ZF M-1375.4 but that is a retailer kit, not a capacity)
fluids.note: No transmission procedure, capacity, fluid number or torque is given here. Do not drain the transmission under the differential steps. A transmission service is a different guide's job and needs the transmission type, which was not proven.

torque.fastener: Rear differential filler/drain plug (screw plug with O-ring, M22x1.5, replace the plug)
torque.conflicts: BMW TIS table: 9AZ oil filler and drain plugs with O-ring (replace plugs) 60 Nm; 3AZ plug with sealing ring 65 Nm. A 5series.net E61 N52 poster states 65 Nm with O-rings and 60 Nm without, which is reversed relative to the TIS table. The TIS table lists E30 to E86 only, not E90.
torque.primaryNote: Primary is the BMW TIS text, applied to the E90 by plug-type match (the OE catalog lists the E90 plug as a screw plug with O-ring); E90 is not named in the TIS table. Independent E90/E9X/F30 secondary sources agree on 60 Nm (44 ft-lb).

torque.fastener: Rear differential plug if it is a sealing-ring (not O-ring) type
torque.conflicts: BMW TIS table 3AZ; not the type listed for this car.

torque.fastener: xDrive transfer case plugs (not applicable to this VIN)
torque.value: MISSING for E90; E53 X5 poster says 33 Nm (24 lb-ft) with 16 mm plugs; E70 X5 poster says 14 mm plugs

torque.fastener: xDrive front differential plug (not applicable to this VIN)
torque.value: MISSING for E90; FCP F30: 60 Nm, 14 mm hex

steps.title: Confirm configuration
steps.instruction: Confirm RWD (the catalog shows no front differential or transfer case for the 328i) and that the rear differential is an open type. If the car is actually xDrive or has an LSD, stop: this guide does not cover them.
warnings: Wrong fluid in an LSD or transfer case can damage it (bavmods; FCP).

steps.title: Level the car and (optionally) warm the fluid
steps.instruction: Park on level ground and support the car securely. A short drive helps the oil flow; one poster warms the new oil in a bowl of warm water. bavmods starts from a cold engine, so this is optional.
warnings: Gear oil and exhaust parts can be hot; follow the jack-stand rule in the safety notes if you raise the car.

steps.title: Loosen the filler plug first
steps.instruction: Before draining anything, loosen the single 14 mm hex plug on the differential housing so you know you can refill. It is both the fill and drain plug on this car. Remove lower braces only if they block access.
warnings: Never remove old oil before confirming the fill plug opens (BMW TIS starts the level check by removing the filler plug).

steps.title: Extract the old fluid through the fill hole
steps.instruction: Pump the old oil out through the fill hole with a suction pump and thin tube, measuring the volume (about 0.95 L reported). Some oil stays behind; one poster did a second drain-and-refill after a week.
warnings: Old gear oil is hazardous; contain and recycle.

steps.title: Refill to the level of the opening
steps.instruction: Pump new SAF-XO 75W-90 GL-5 synthetic through the fill hole until it just trickles out (the level is the lower edge of the filler opening). Expect about 1.0 L on the N52; the level, not the volume, decides.
warnings: Use only BMW-approved gear oil; do not use 75W-140 unless the car has an LSD.

steps.title: Fit a new plug and torque it
steps.instruction: Clean the opening, fit a new screw plug with O-ring (33117525064) and tighten to 60 Nm (44 ft-lb). If the plug is reused, inspect the O-ring; BMW TIS says replace O-ring plugs.
warnings: Do not exceed the torque (do not use the 65 Nm sealing-ring value on an O-ring plug).
One E60 poster reports the opposite assignment of 60/65 Nm; the TIS table prevails.

steps.title: Clean, test drive, recheck
steps.instruction: Wipe the housing clean, refit any braces, take a short drive listening for noise or shudder, then check for seepage around the plug.

steps.title: xDrive only: transfer case and front differential (NOT for this VIN)
steps.instruction: Not applicable to a RWD 328i. Reference only: transfer case DTF-1 about 1 L, open the fill plug first, drain, refill to overflow; E70/E53 plug sizes differ (14 mm vs 16 mm) and no E90 torque was found. Front differential plug locations/torque for the E90 were not found.
warnings: Do not apply F30, E53 or E70 values to an E90.

safety: Always confirm the fill plug can be removed before draining.

Never work under, or take a wheel off, a car held only by a jack. Support it on rated jack stands on hard, level ground, or use a lift or drive-on ramps where the job allows. Use the jacking points shown in the jacking illustration in your owner's manual, with a pad or adapter between the jack and the plastic pad. If you cannot identify a safe place for the stand from your manual, stop and use a shop lift.
Use only BMW-approved synthetic gear oil (SAF-XO 75W-90 GL-5 for open diffs).
Use 60 Nm only for an O-ring plug and replace the plug; the sealing-ring plug value is 65 Nm per TIS.
Contain and recycle used gear oil.
Do not apply xDrive or other-chassis values to this car.
Do not drain or open the automatic transmission as part of this job; the transmission fluid is a separate sealed system and is not covered here.
missingEvidence: BMW document with the rear differential capacity for the E90 328i (TIS text gives only the level rule).
BMW service interval (BMW training says lifetime-fill; others give 40,000-60,000 mi).
E90-specific lower-brace and plug access detail (bimmerpost E93 poster only).
xDrive front differential and transfer case values for the E90: NOT APPLICABLE to this RWD 328i; intentionally not researched.
A copy of the BMW TIS page that names the E90 for the 60 Nm plug torque (the table available lists E30-E86).
Open differential is probable on four independent lines of evidence but no BMW document or E90 328i build sheet states 'open'; if a BMW TIS option page is later obtained, upgrade.
Transmission model (GA6L45R vs GA6HP19Z) and any automatic-transmission fluid values: out of scope of this guide, left unresolved on purpose.

visuals.title: Rear differential single fill/drain plug

elements.describe: The rear differential housing (type 188L) seen from underneath, with a bolted cover.
A single large M22x1.5 screw plug with a 14 mm internal hex that serves as both fill and drain.
Lower chassis braces that can leave little room to turn the plug.

facts.note: OE catalog: one screw plug with O-ring M22x1.5; bimmersport: one drain/fill bolt for both; bavmods: the fill plug also serves as the drain; bimmerpost 335d: no drain plug.
No fetched source states where on the housing the plug sits (side, rear cover). GAP: show the plug generically without a precise face.
OE catalog: final drive TYP 188L with a transmission cover and hex bolts; BMW training doc: 188L final drive.
E93 328i poster only: no room to loosen or tighten the plug because of the lower braces.

mustNotDepict.reason: Position on the housing is not established; do not mark it on a specific side or the cover.
No second plug: the E90 rear differential has one plug only.

https://www.realoem.com/bmw/enUS/showpar.establishes: OE catalog final drive gasket set for this 328i: cover TYP 188L, 8 hex bolts, one screw plug with O-ring M22x1.5 (33117525064), shaft seals.
OE catalog rear-axle-drive 188L; ratio 3.23 or 3.73 (automatic); synthetic gear oil 1 L.

https://archive.org/download/BMWTechnica.establishes: BMW training doc: the final drive is the 188L unit; lifetime-fill oil.

https://bimmersport.co.nz/topic/60049-e9.establishes: E90 335i: 14 mm hex plug, no drain plug, pump oil out through the fill hole.

https://bavmods.com/pages/how-to-change-.establishes: E9X: 14 mm Allen, fill plug is also the drain, 44 lb-ft.

https://5series.net/forums/topic/126110-.establishes: E61 N52: plugs need a 14 mm hex; torque posts.

https://g42.bimmerpost.com/forums/showth.establishes: E90 thread: 335d has no drain plug; fluid pumped from the fill hole.
E93 328i: lower braces block access to the plug; crowfoot with Allen used.

https://www.fcpeuro.com/blog/how-to-repl.establishes: F30: 14 mm hex bit plug, 60 Nm (different chassis, same plug size).

gapFillNotes: fill-drain-plug location NOT established: bimmersport, bavmods, m3post, z4-forum, 5series.net threads, the BMW TIS pdf and bimmerpost threads were all fetched and none states which face/side of the 188L housing the plug is on (only that it is reached from underneath the rear of the car, with little room because of the lower braces/reinforcement plate). Web search budget ran out before a RealOEM-diagram or photo-description source could be found. Draw the plug generically on the housing.

visuals.title: Filling to the level of the opening

elements.describe: The open fill hole with the oil level at its lower edge; oil trickles out when the differential is full.
A thin tube from a hand pump or squeeze bottle pressed into the opening.
A suction tube used earlier to pump old oil out through the same opening.

facts.note: TIS: fill to the lower edge of the filler plug opening; bimmersport: until a small trickle runs out; bavmods: a slow steady stream; xoutpost: pump in until it begins to overflow.
Hand pump or squeeze-bottle nozzle pressed into the fill hole.
Old oil is extracted through the fill hole with a suction pump.
No source describes the opening geometry or internal level marks. GAP: show a simple opening without internal detail.

bimmersport (E90 335i) says old fluid is suctioned out via the fill plug / fill hole; bavmods (E9x) says the pump nozzle is pressed into the fill plug hole; the BMW TIS pdf also refers to oil being filled to the lower edge of the filler opening.

bavmods: easy-fill hand pump whose nozzle goes into the hole and a two-way transfer pump hose; bimmersport: a tube is guided into the fill hole to suck fluid out; xoutpost (X5 E70): tube on a large syringe and a pump.
Both say the tube/nozzle enters the differential through the fill plug hole (placed plainly: tube end in the fill opening); neither states which face of the housing.
NOT established: no fetched page states which side/face of the rear differential housing the fill hole is on, only that it is reached from underneath. Draw generically on the housing.

mustNotDepict.reason: Internal geometry and housing shape around the opening are not established.

https://5series.net/forums/attachments/d.establishes: BMW TIS text: add oil until it reaches the lower edge of the filler plug opening; use only approved oils.

https://bimmersport.co.nz/topic/60049-e9.establishes: Pump out via the fill hole; fill until a small trickle runs out with the car level.

https://bavmods.com/pages/how-to-change-.establishes: Two-way transfer pump and easy-fill pump; fill until a slow steady stream.

https://xoutpost.com/bmw-sav-forums/x5-e.establishes: X5 E70: extract and refill through the fill holes with syringe/tube.

gapFillNotes: fill-opening location unresolved (see above); search budget ran out.

resolutionNotes: RESOLVED: open vs limited-slip. Four lines: OE catalog (single 188L assembly, ratio variants only), VIN decode (no LSD option), Turner (BMW stopped true limited-slip on E9X; only a ratio swap is sold for 325i/328i/330i), BimmerWorld (3.73 for 328i is an open carrier; LSDs are a separate upgrade). Status: open, probable. No owner inspection needed; step 1 remains a stop sign for a mis-identified car.

RESOLVED: final-drive ratio question. Catalog 3.73 with automatic (S205A) and 3.23 otherwise; BimmerWorld stock 3.23; Turner manual 3.15 or 3.23. The suggested 3.46 does not appear in any retrievable source and is not asserted. It is identification-only; fluid, plug and torque do not depend on it.

RESOLVED: automatic transmission fluid is a separate sealed unit and is not part of the differential job (new fluids row, CONFLICT: BMW 'lifetime' vs ZF 50,000 mi/8 yr and GM under 45,000 mi). Transmission model (GA6L45R vs GA6HP19Z) is UNRESOLVED: ECS lists both for the E90 328i N52 and BimmerWorld ties GA6L45R to 328i from 9/2008, so GA6L45R is likely for the 09/2009 build but unproven. No transmission procedure or number is added.

RESOLVED (applicability): xDrive transfer case and front differential rows are NOT APPLICABLE (RWD 328i: NHTSA decode, catalog without front axle, decoder). Kept as reference with a stop warning; not researched further.
RESOLVED: jack stand tool row gained E90 jacking sources (generic safety equipment).

NOT RESOLVED: capacity. 1.0 L for N52 per bimmerpost, bimmersport, 5series; 1.2 L for N54/335i/diesel and one generic E9X article. No BMW number (TIS gives only the level rule), so fill to the lower edge of the filler opening and treat 1.0 L as an estimate.

NOT RESOLVED: service interval (BMW training: lifetime fill; retailers 40,000-60,000 mi / 75,000-100,000 km) and the E90-named TIS torque table. 60 Nm (O-ring plug, replace plug) stays VERIFIED via the BMW TIS text applied by plug-type match plus three E90/E9X/F30 secondary hosts; the 65 Nm sealing-ring value is not the type listed for this car.
NOT RESOLVED: lower-brace access on the E90 (bimmerpost E93 poster only); step 3 already says to remove braces only if they block the plug and gives the snub-nose 14 mm hex or crowfoot workaround.
